 Gukesh and Sindarov set for World Championship showdown
 Thursday, 19 Nov 2026 
 UTC +1 
 12:15 
 Share this post: 
 CHESS NEWS 
 Tags: 
 FIDE World Championship Match 
 The Salesforce FIDE World Championship Match 2026 is set to make history as the youngest encounter for the classical world title. Both contenders are still in their early twenties, brimming with energy and ambition, and with much of their chess careers still ahead of them.
 Beyond the generational aspect, the match also brings together representatives of two of the world’s leading chess nations. Reigning World Champion Gukesh Dommaraju has followed in the footsteps of India’s legendary Viswanathan Anand , whose achievements and world title triumph in 2000 helped spark the country’s chess boom. His challenger, Javokhir Sindarov , represents the remarkable new generation of Uzbek talent, nurtured in a country where chess enjoys strong institutional and government support.
 The champion 
 At just 20, Gukesh is preparing to defend his world title for the first time. The Indian prodigy has rewritten the record books on numerous occasions, establishing himself as one of the most precocious talents in chess history. He became a Grandmaster at the age of 12, won individual gold medals at the Chess Olympiads 2022 and 2024, and became the youngest-ever winner of the Candidates Tournament in 2024. Later that year, he faced Ding Liren in the World Championship Match in Singapore. In a tense and closely fought encounter, Gukesh clinched the title with a victory in the decisive final game. At 18, he became the youngest undisputed classical World Champion in history.
 Photo: Michal Walusza 
 Since that remarkable achievement, however, maintaining his exceptional level of performance has proved challenging. His more recent results have been below expectations, and his rating has dipped to 2710, leaving him 26th in the world rankings. Gukesh’s main task ahead of the match will be to rediscover his best form – or perhaps, more importantly, find a fresh source of inspiration to propel him back to the top.
 The challenger 
 Sindarov is only a few months older than his opponent, and his career already features several comparable milestones. Like Gukesh, he became a Grandmaster at the age of 12 and has also tasted success at the Chess Olympiads.
 In April 2026, the young Uzbek produced a superb performance to win the Candidates Tournament in Cyprus, becoming the first player from his country to qualify for a classical World Championship Match. He is clearly enjoying a remarkable run of form and currently occupies fourth place in the world rankings, having reached a career-high rating of 2782.
 Photo: Michal Walusza 
 Given the contrasting trajectories of the two contenders, many observers regard Sindarov as the favourite going into the match. Their head-to-head record also gives the challenger an edge: Sindarov leads 2.5–0.5 in their classical encounters. However, both of those victories date back to 2018 and 2022, when the players were still very young. Their most recent encounter in Wijk aan Zee earlier this year ended in a draw after Sindarov managed to escape from a lost position. 
 The match 
 The match will consist of 14 classical games. The first player to score 7.5 points or more will be crowned World Champion and claim the larger share of the total prize fund of USD 2.5 million. Each game will feature a time control of 120 minutes for the first 40 moves, followed by 30 minutes for the rest of the game, with a 30-second increment from move 41 onwards. If the match ends in a tie after 14 games, a rapid-play tie-break will determine the champion.
 Salesforce will serve as the Title Partner, with Freedom as General Partner of the upcoming World Championship Match. The event will take place in Geneva, Switzerland, from November 22 to December 12, with the first game scheduled for November 24. Switzerland has a long tradition of hosting major events in the World Championship cycle. Highlights include the legendary 1953 Candidates Tournament in Zurich and Neuhausen, several Candidates Matches during the 1970s and 1980s, the Interzonal Tournaments in Biel (1976, 1985, and 1993), and the 2004 World Championship Match between Vladimir Kramnik and Peter Leko in Brissago.
 The playing venue is the Fondation Martin Bodmer in Cologny, overlooking Lake Geneva. This unique cultural institution and museum is dedicated to preserving and showcasing one of the world’s most remarkable collections of manuscripts, rare books, and historical documents that trace the evolution of human thought and literature.
 Written by Yannick Pelletier 
 The Salesforce FIDE World Championship Match 2026 is taking place at the Fondation Martin Bodmer in Cologny, near Geneva, Switzerland, from November 22 to December 12. The first round will be played on November 24. All information on the schedule can be found on the Championship website . Tickets to the playing hall and the fan zone can be purchased on the designated website: https://tickets.fide.com/en , while games can be watched on the FIDE YouTube channel with live commentaries by top Grandmasters Peter Leko and Peter Svidler .
